extracted.intended_audience: People of the State of New York / citizens deciding on ratification of the U.S. Constitution
extracted.subtask_description: Normative criteria and practical principles for structuring federal and state powers (especially militia regulation and taxation) advanced to guide ratification debates and constitutional design. Focuses on how powers should be apportioned, limited, and implemented to secure liberty and effective government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual checks between general and state governments
rubrics_metrics.description: Power being almost always the rival of power, the general government will at all times stand ready to check the usurpations of the state governments, and these will have the same disposition towards the general government. The people, by throwing themselves into either scale, will infallibly make it preponderate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cherish the union so the people can use one level of government as an instrument of redress against incursions by the other; institutional rivalry plus popular engagement preserves liberty.

rubrics_metrics.name: State governments as a security against national usurpation
rubrics_metrics.description: The State governments will, in all possible contingencies, afford complete security against invasions of the public liberty by the national authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State legislatures, having better information and local organs of power and the confidence of the people, can detect danger earlier, adopt organized opposition, communicate with other states, and combine resources to protect common liberty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical extent as a guard against consolidation of power
rubrics_metrics.description: The great extent of the country is a further security... If the federal army should be able to quell the resistance of one State, the distant States would have it in their power to make head with fresh forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large territory and dispersed populations make it costly and difficult for a central authority to impose despotism; advances in one place would be offset by renewed resistance elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military force will be limited by national resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent of the military force must, at all events, be regulated by the resources of the country... For a long time to come, it will not be possible to maintain a large army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because maintaining a large standing army is expensive, practical resource limits and population growth naturally constrain the federal capacity to sustain a force capable of erecting a despotism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity in militia organization is desirable for effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Uniformity in the organization and discipline of the militia would be attended with the most beneficial effects, whenever they were called into service for the public defense. It would enable them to discharge the duties of the camp and of the field with mutual intelligence and concert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such uniformity is best accomplished by confiding regulation of the militia to the national authority so that units can operate together effectively in defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal power to organize, arm, and discipline militia with state appointment of officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Empower the Union 'to provide for organizing, arming, and disciplining the militia, and for governing such part of them as may be employed in the service of the United States, RESERVING TO THE STATES RESPECTIVELY THE APPOINTMENT OF THE OFFICERS, AND THE AUTHORITY OF TRAINING THE MILITIA ACCORDING TO THE DISCIPLINE PRESCRIBED BY CONGRESS.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National oversight should secure uniformity while reserving officer appointment and state training authority to preserve local influence and guard against federal misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: An efficacious militia power reduces the need for standing armies
rubrics_metrics.description: If standing armies are dangerous to liberty, an efficacious power over the militia ... ought, as far as possible, to take away the inducement and the pretext to such unfriendly institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting the Union authority over militia service in emergencies provides a substitute for standing armies and thus a safeguard for liberty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal authority can require citizen aid when necessary (posse comitatus implication)
rubrics_metrics.description: A right to pass all laws NECESSARY AND PROPER to execute its declared powers, would include that of requiring the assistance of the citizens to the officers who may be intrusted with the execution of those laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The absence of an explicit posse comitatus clause does not imply inability to call for citizen assistance; such powers are implied where necessary and proper to execute federal duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid disciplining the entire militia—impracticable and burdensome
rubrics_metrics.description: The project of disciplining all the militia of the United States is as futile as it would be injurious... To oblige the great body of the yeomanry... to be under arms... would be a real grievance to the people, and a serious public inconvenience and loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit training obligations for the general populace to modest requirements (e.g., being armed and assembled once or twice a year) to avoid undue burden on productive labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form a select, well-trained corps rather than discipline the whole people
rubrics_metrics.description: It is of the utmost importance that a well-digested plan should... be adopted for the proper establishment of the militia... to the formation of a select corps of moderate extent, upon such principles as will really fit them for service in case of need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circumscribing training to a moderate select body produces an excellent, ready force that diminishes the need for standing armies and strengthens defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of militia officers by states secures local influence and counters federal danger
rubrics_metrics.description: What reasonable cause of apprehension can be inferred... while the particular States are to have the SOLE AND EXCLUSIVE APPOINTMENT OF THE OFFICERS? If it were possible seriously to indulge a jealousy... the circumstance of the officers being in the appointment of the States ought at once to extinguish it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State appointment of officers preserves a preponderating local influence over the militia and mitigates fears of federal misuse of militia forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: National government must have a general power of taxation
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be interwoven, in the frame of the government, a general power of taxation, in one shape or another... It must embrace a provision for the support of the national civil list; for the payment of the national debts... and, in general, for all those matters which will call for disbursements out of the national treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxation power must cover military expenses, civil establishment costs, national debt, and any other national disbursements to ensure an effective government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Money is the vital principle of government; revenue must be regular and adequate
rubrics_metrics.description: Money is, with propriety, considered as the vital principle of the body politic... A complete power, therefore, to procure a regular and adequate supply of it... may be regarded as an indispensable ingredient in every constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Without reliable revenue, government either plunders the people or atrophies; sound constitutions must enable consistent provisioning of public needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requisition/quota system is inadequate; national government must raise its own revenues
rubrics_metrics.description: The present Confederation... permits Congress to call for sums... but in practice it has been constantly exercised, and would continue to be so, as long as the revenues of the Confederacy should remain dependent on the intermediate agency of its members... What remedy can there be for this situation, but in a change of the system... permitting the national government to raise its own revenues by the ordinary methods of taxation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependence on state requisitions undermines national finances and cohesion; direct federal taxation provides stability and creditworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject artificial internal/external taxation distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: The more intelligent adversaries... qualify their admission by a distinction between what they call INTERNAL and EXTERNAL taxation... This distinction, however, would violate the maxim of good sense and sound policy, which dictates that every POWER ought to be in proportion to its OBJECT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limiting federal taxation to external duties would be insufficient for national needs; taxation authority should be aligned with the object to be achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers must be commensurate with their objects; means proportioned to ends
rubrics_metrics.description: A government ought to contain in itself every power requisite to the full accomplishment of the objects committed to its care... the means ought to be proportioned to the end; that every power ought to be commensurate with its object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional powers should be framed so they can effectively achieve their purposes; unpredictable exigencies justify broad authority to provide for national defense and other unbounded needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation power enables borrowing and secures public credit
rubrics_metrics.description: The power of creating new funds upon new objects of taxation, by its own authority, would enable the national government to borrow as far as its necessities might require... Foreigners, as well as the citizens of America, could then reasonably repose confidence in its engagements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A government's ability to tax underpins its credit; without independent revenue-raising, borrowing would be limited and costly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections about federal taxation depriving states are political, not purely constitutional
rubrics_metrics.description: To say that deficiencies may be provided for by requisitions upon the States... is on the one hand to acknowledge that this system cannot be depended upon... It ought to be recollected that if less will be required from the States, they will have proportionably less means to answer the demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns that federal taxation will crush state finances misunderstand how powers ought to relate to objects; composition and structure of government and popular vigilance are better safeguards than limiting federal powers.
